## How Sessions 11–13 fit together

| Session | Responsibility | Lab output |
|---|---|---|
| [11 · Functions](../session11/index.qmd) | Define one operation and its contract | Conditions, a small function, and a checked refactor |
| [12 · Reliability](../session12/index.qmd) | Diagnose failures and preserve repairs | Reprex, repaired functions, regression checks |
| [13 · Iteration](../session13/index.qmd) | Repeat checked operations and compare implementations | Named results with equivalence and performance evidence |

These sessions complete the core R programming sequence. Later statistical
and topic-specific sessions build on these tools. Each lab includes its own
synthetic inputs and supplied prerequisites, so it can run in a fresh session.

## Session outline and content

### 1. Conditions

Begin with unequal-length paired measurements: R can silently recycle values
and produce incorrect changes. Use `if` to check whether calculation may proceed, then
repair a vector condition using `ifelse()` for row labels or `any()`/`all()` for
a group decision. Treat missing and empty conditions separately before practice.

### 2. Why functions?

Identify duplicated calculations and state inputs, options, outputs, and edge cases.

### 3. Function basics

Read an existing function call: package namespace, function name, parameters,
supplied arguments, and return value. Connect these to Usage, Arguments, and
Value in its help page. Build a summary from a checked calculation, identify
required inputs and options, trace a call, and check changed inputs. Extend the
helper with an observed count, missing count, and explicit missing-data policy.
Use explicit `return()` calls and `invisible()` when automatic printing is
unwanted. Practice one four-component summary and extract results by name.

### 4. Scope

Replace hidden global dependencies with explicit arguments.

### 5. Validation

Use guard clauses and enforce the safe-mean and scalar-center contracts. Trace
the first exit for invalid, all-missing, empty, and ordinary inputs.

### 6. Data-frame functions

Check columns and distinguish quoted-name extraction from bare-name dplyr interfaces.

### 7. Refactoring and reuse

Compose paired-change helpers and compare against hand-built and original results.
Save reusable definitions in R scripts, load them with `source()`, and verify
the report in a fresh session.

### 8. Exit check

Explain the contract and the evidence that intended behavior was preserved.
